name: Ramp
text: I think we should make a decision to prioritize high contrast ratios between background and foreground elements, as this will greatly improve readability for users with visual impairments. By doing so, we're accepting the trade-off that our design might not look as sleek or modern, as high contrast ratios can sometimes be perceived as less visually appealing. However, this decision is crucial for making EXCAVA usable by everyone, especially for users who rely heavily on visual cues. By prioritizing accessibility over aesthetics, we're ensuring that our platform is inclusive and usable for a wider range of users.

name: Reader
text: As I tab through the proposed design, I'm concerned that prioritizing high contrast ratios alone might not be enough, as it may not address issues with keyboard navigation and screen reader compatibility. A better alternative could be to implement a more comprehensive accessibility framework that includes features like semantic HTML, ARIA attributes, and customizable font sizes, which would provide a more inclusive experience for all users. To settle the argument, I'd like to see some user testing with screen readers and keyboard-only navigation to determine the most effective approach.
